components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; padding: 20px 40px; background: rgba(3,3,4,0.85); backdrop-filter: blur(10px); border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.05); } .ds-nav-brand { font-family: 'Syncopate', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 1.2rem; letter-spacing: 2px; color: #fff; } .ds-nav-links { display: flex; gap: 30px; } .ds-nav-links a { position: relative; color: #989898; font-family: 'Space Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.9rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 1px; text-decoration: none; transition: 0.3s; } .ds-nav-links a::after { content: ''; position: absolute; bottom: -5px; left: 0; width: 0; height: 1px; background: #c5a059; transition: 0.3s; } .ds-nav-links a:hover, .ds-nav-links a:focus-visible { color: #c5a059; outline: none; } .ds-nav-links a:hover::after, .ds-nav-links a:focus-visible::after { width: 100%; } .ds-nav-links a.ds-nav-gold { color: #c5a059; }

narrative.overview:
The site is an astronaut's heads-up display at the edge of Gargantua. A near-black void fills the screen, with a slow particle field and a radial vignette that darkens the edges like a gravity well. On top of it, thin-bordered instrument panels carry the content: gold readouts, cyan data signals, monospace telemetry. Its references are Interstellar (the quote, the video, the tesseract side nav) and The Matrix (a hidden mode that hides the content and fills the screen with falling green code).

The mood is cinematic. Type is wide and spaced out for headlines and monospace for everything else, so the whole page reads like instrument output. Labels are in uppercase system language ("SYSTEM ONLINE", "ARCHIVE ACCESS", "TEMPORAL LOG"). Density is low: each section takes a full viewport and the content sits inside a 1200px column with generous space around it.

Interaction is where the panels come alive. At rest they are dark, translucent glass. When the cursor arrives (a custom gold dot with a trailing ring), borders light up gold or cyan, panels lift a few pixels and coloured light spills out.
keyCharacteristics: Void-black canvas with a live particle field and an edge vignette
Syncopate for display, Space Mono for everything else
Gold for action and identity, cyan for knowledge and data, green only in Matrix mode
Glass at rest, coloured glow on interaction
Custom cursor on desktop, native cursor on touch

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: Each accent means one thing. Gold is action and identity, cyan is knowledge and data, green is Matrix mode only, red is alarm only. Don't use cyan on a CTA or gold on an education entry.

rules.name: The Void Base Rule
rules.body: Every surface is the void plus transparency (rgba(15,15,20,0.6), rgba(20,20,25,0.4)), never a lighter solid grey. Panels let the particle field show through.

rules.name: The Telemetry Rule
rules.body: If text isn't a headline, it's in Space Mono. Syncopate never sets a paragraph.

rules.name: The Slash Rule
rules.body: Labels separate their parts with // or | ("SYSTEM ONLINE // PORTUGAL", "WebDev | Networking | Cybersecurity"), never bullets or commas.

rules.name: The Light-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Elevation is shown with coloured light, not grey drop shadows. If a panel needs to come forward, it glows in its accent.

dos: Do set every surface as void plus transparency, and let the particle field show through.
Do keep corners square (0px) on panels and buttons; 2–4px only on tiny chips and badges.
Do use Gargantua Gold for action and identity, and Tesseract Cyan for knowledge and data (the One Job Rule).
Do use the physics ease (cubic-bezier(0.19, 1, 0.22, 1)) for movement such as panels and the header.
Do write labels in uppercase HUD language with // separators.
Do use the :root tokens; the current hard-coded #fff, #aaa, #666 and #ff4444 (the breach button, which differs from --error #ff3333) are drift to fold back into tokens.
donts: Don't use grey drop shadows for elevation; use coloured light.
Don't use Matrix Green outside Matrix mode and the status light.
Don't fill surfaces with solid lighter greys; they break the void.
